Daily Brief

The most consequential development today is the White House confirmation that President Trump will hold a historic trilateral summit with Presidents Xi Jinping and Putin on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen next week [BBC], [Al Jazeera]. The meeting comes as Ukraine's President Zelensky revealed that US negotiators have floated the idea of Kyiv ceding the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership—a proposal he said would require a referendum [BBC], [Le Monde], [Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, the FAA lifted the longest nationwide ground stop since 9/11 after a communication system failure grounded US flights for over four hours, causing more than 16,000 delays and cancellations [BBC], [Globe and Mail]. Transportation Secretary Duffy blamed aging infrastructure and called for $50 billion in modernization funding. In France, a fifth consecutive Saturday of protests drew tens of thousands to the streets over cost-of-living concerns, child protection measures, and police conduct [RFI]. South Sudan postponed its first-ever national elections from December to February amid escalating ethnic tensions [RFI], [Al Jazeera]. In Hungary, authorities uncovered nearly $20 million in cash hidden across the country as part of an anti-corruption probe into a former Orbán-era minister [BBC Europe].

01 Geopolitics

Trump, Putin, and Xi to Hold Historic Trilateral Summit at APEC in China

  • The White House confirmed that President Trump will meet with Presidents Putin and Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, from November 18-19
  • Nuclear weapons proliferation will be the primary topic; Iran may also be discussed, but Ukraine is not expected to be on the agenda
  • No formal agreement is expected from the talks; Moscow and Beijing have not yet commented on the announcement
  • This will be Trump's fourth meeting with Xi since returning to office in January 2025

02 Geopolitics

Zelensky Says US Floated Ukraine Ceding Donbas for NATO Membership

  • Ukrainian President Zelensky disclosed that US negotiators raised the possibility of Ukraine withdrawing forces from the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership
  • Zelensky said this was the first time such a proposal had been raised by US officials during talks in Abu Dhabi this week
  • Zelensky stated he would put any proposal with security guarantees, no military constraints, and reconstruction funds to a national referendum
  • Russia's position reportedly remains unchanged, with Moscow demanding both territorial concessions and Ukrainian neutrality

03 Technology

FAA Lifts Longest US Ground Stop Since 9/11 After Communication System Failure

  • The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop lasting over four hours on Friday due to communication issues affecting all air traffic control centers
  • More than 8,500 flights were delayed and nearly 8,000 cancelled; approximately 3,500 planes were airborne when the order was issued
  • Transportation Secretary Duffy blamed aging infrastructure with technology from the 1970s-1990s and called for $50 billion in modernization funding
  • Homeland Security confirmed the issue arose during system patch application; no evidence of cyberattack or terrorism was found

04 Society

France Faces Fifth Consecutive Saturday of Nationwide Protests

  • Between 30,000 and 60,000 demonstrators expected in Paris alone, with 50-60 marches planned nationwide
  • Protests encompass cost-of-living concerns, child protection measures, and opposition to a new police protection bill
  • What began as high school student protests over deteriorating school conditions has expanded to include university students, unions, and broader public
  • Some 70,000 police and gendarmes have been deployed; allegations of police brutality have helped galvanize wider support for the movement

05 Policy

South Sudan Delays First National Elections Until February Amid Rising Tensions

  • South Sudan's electoral commission postponed presidential and legislative elections from December 22 to February 11, 2027
  • The announcement came on the day voter registration was scheduled to begin; no official reason was given for the delay
  • Former Vice President Riek Machar has been under house arrest since March 2025, accused of crimes against humanity
  • The elections have been delayed at least three times since 2022; the UN had warned that a December vote could trigger widespread conflict
